summary.text: Abyssal plains are flat, smooth stretches of deep ocean floor, usually lying 3,000 to 6,000 metres down.
They form when fine clay and silt, much of it carried by turbidity currents down submarine canyons, blanket the uneven crust made by seafloor spreading.
They cover more than half of Earth's surface, yet darkness and water pressure of up to about 750 times atmospheric pressure leave them poorly explored.

facts.label: Metals in nodules
facts.value: Manganese, iron, nickel, cobalt and copper

items.prompt: Counting land and sea together, roughly how much of Earth's whole surface do abyssal plains cover?
items.explain: Abyssal plains cover more than 50% of Earth's surface.

items.prompt: The ocean crust under an abyssal plain is bumpy, yet the plain on top is very smooth. Why?

options.label: Fine sediment has settled over the bumps
Deep currents have ground the rock flat
Lava spread out and cooled in a flat sheet
Old ice sheets scraped the bottom level

items.explain: Abyssal plains come from fine clay and silt blanketing an originally uneven surface of ocean crust.

items.prompt: Fish that thrive in surface waters would struggle to live on an abyssal plain. What does the water there lack?
items.explain: Because oxygen is scarce, abyssal plains are inhospitable to organisms that would do well in the oxygen-rich waters above.

items.prompt: Geologists find very few ancient abyssal plains preserved in old rock layers. Why?
items.explain: Abyssal plains tend to be consumed by subduction, so they are poorly preserved in the sedimentary record.

items.prompt: Much of the mud on abyssal plains starts at the edges of the continents. How does most of it reach the deep floor?

options.label: Glaciers push it along the seabed
Turbidity currents carry it down canyons
Lava flows sweep it out to sea

items.explain: Much of the sediment is deposited by turbidity currents channelled from continental margins along submarine canyons into deeper water.

items.prompt: A biologist wants to predict what kind of animal community lives on a patch of abyssal plain. What should she measure first?

options.label: How much food sinks down and what it is
How much sunlight reaches the bottom
How tall the waves are at the surface
How far away the nearest island is

items.explain: The structure of abyssal ecosystems is strongly shaped by how fast food falls to the seafloor and what that settling material is made of.
